title: Attention lane adapter and kernel negotiator
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Kernel choice for attention-heavy models varies dramatically across sequence length, kv-cache state (prefill vs decode), and hardware generation. Existing heuristics are static and either over-prioritize p50 latency (hurting cost) or p95 (hurting throughput). Goal: Implement an "attention lane" abstraction plus a lightweight runtime negotiator that adaptively routes requests to kernel lanes and scheduling strategies to minimize p95 latency under cost constraints while preserving decode throughput and avoiding KV cache churn.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Negotiator routes >= 95% of inference requests to an appropriate kernel lane without manual rule flips. 2) Measured improvement: >=15% p95 reduction on mixed workloads (seqlen 32/128/512) on A100 and T4 compared to current static policy; cost-per-token change <= +5%. 3) Safe rollout with canary toggles and automatic fallback to baseline on error/latency regressions.
design_notes: Architecture: define three attention lanes: SHORT (seqlen <= 64, tiled fused kernels), MID (65-512, flash-attention variants with windowing options), LONG (>512, chunked streaming + kernel fallback). The negotiator is a small runtime decision function that consumes features: gpu_family, free_mem_bytes, estimated_kv_size, request_seqlen, temperature, model_variant, and recent latency quantiles. Policy: contextual UCB-style weight with decaying exploration and fast warm-start from offline microbenchmarks. Prefill vs Decode: treat prefill as a special vectorized lane that prioritizes throughput and memory packing; decode lane prioritizes low tail latency and KV cache reuse. Fallthrough: if chosen kernel fails or exceeds soft-latency threshold, automatically switch to fallback lane and emit telemetry.
experiment_summary: Microbench (internal trace replay): mixed traffic with 40% seqlen 32, 40% seqlen 128, 20% seqlen 512. Baseline: static policy (flash for mid+long, tiled for short). Negotiator (initial config) results on A100: p50 unchanged, p95 reduced by 22% for decode-heavy runs, cost-per-token +2%. On T4: p95 reduced by 18%, throughput for large-prefill improved by 12% due to better packing. Observed edge-case: when GPU free memory < 1.5GB, negotiator preferred small-kernel lanes that increased kernel launch overhead; we added a memory threshold feature to avoid regressions.
risks_and_tradeoffs: - Additional decision latency (negotiator must be <200us) — implemented as inline heuristic + cached recent decisions. - Complexity of rollout: many kernel variants and per-arch behavior requires staged gatekeeping and a metrics-driven rollback. - Risk of cache fragmentation if negotiator frequently switches lanes for same session; mitigated with sticky decisions per session for the first N tokens.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype negotiator as a pluggable runtime module (week 1). 2) Add offline microbench harness for new lane combos and store warm-start priors (week 1-2). 3) Implement sticky-session binding and memory-threshold guards (week 2). 4) Canary rollout to 5% of traffic with detailed p95/cost dashboards (week 3). 5) Collect metrics for 1 week, iterate, then full rollout (week 4).
